title: U.S. House · Texas's 35th District
area: A South-Central Texas district including parts of San Antonio.

context.text: Texas redrew its congressional map for the 2026 election cycle. This is an open seat with no incumbent on the general-election ballot; Rep. Greg Casar, who represented a differently drawn 35th District, is instead running for re-election in the redrawn 37th District. Johnny Garcia defeated Maureen Galindo in the Democratic primary runoff, and Carlos De La Cruz defeated John Lujan in the Republican primary runoff.

candidates.name: Johnny Garcia
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Democratic primary runoff against Maureen Galindo
candidates.currentRole: Former Bexar County Sheriff's Office deputy and SWAT hostage negotiator

summary.text: Johnny Garcia is a former Bexar County Sheriff's Office deputy, SWAT hostage negotiator, and public information officer from San Antonio's West Side, running as a Democrat focused on lowering costs and affordable health care.

background.text: Born and raised in San Antonio's West Side; graduated from Memorial High School and attended St. Philip's College.
Worked in construction before spending nearly two decades at the Bexar County Sheriff's Office, including as a SWAT hostage negotiator and public information officer.

priorities.text: Says he is fighting for lower costs, affordable health care, and economic opportunity for working families in TX-35.
priorities.quote: An old school Democrat, Johnny is fighting for the working families in TX-35 — for lower costs, affordable healthcare, and the chance to get ahead.

positions.summary: Campaign describes him as fighting for affordable health care for working families.
positions.quote: for lower costs, affordable healthcare, and the chance to get ahead

candidates.name: Carlos De La Cruz
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Republican primary runoff against John Lujan
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Air Force veteran; small business owner

summary.text: Carlos De La Cruz is a 20-year U.S. Air Force veteran who deployed to Afghanistan, Iraq, and the U.S.-Mexico border, and who co-founded a kickboxing gym in San Antonio with his wife after leaving the military.

background.text: Served 20 years in the U.S. Air Force, deploying to Afghanistan, Iraq, and the border with Mexico.
Co-founded a kickboxing gym in San Antonio with his wife, a VA nurse practitioner, after leaving the Air Force.

priorities.text: Supports continued efforts to secure the border and equip Border Patrol agents.
Supports holding the Mexican government accountable for water deliveries owed to Texas agricultural communities under treaty obligations.
Says he will support President Trump's agenda in Congress, including on manufacturing and trade with China.

positions.summary: Supports continuing to secure the border and providing Border Patrol agents more resources.
positions.quote: We need to continue securing our border and ensure our Border Patrol agents have the tools, manpower, and support they deserve.

positions.summary: Supports trade measures aimed at stopping China from what he describes as unfair trade practices, as part of an "America First" platform.
positions.quote: stopping communist China from ripping us off
